q: The arrangement of electrons in an atom was suggested in 1913 by ____.
e: Niels Bohr proposed the model of electrons orbiting the nucleus in specific energy levels.

q: Electrons move round the nucleus in definite shells or ____.
e: Bohr's model describes electrons traveling in fixed circular paths around the nucleus.

q: Each shell is numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on, going outwards from the ____.
e: Shell numbers increase as the distance from the central nucleus increases.

q: They are also known as K shell, L shell, M shell, N shell, and so on, as shown in Figure 3.3, with the first being the ____ shell.
e: The innermost shell (n=1) is designated as the K shell.

q: In general, the closer the shell is to the nucleus, the lower is its ____.
e: Electrons in inner shells are more tightly bound and possess lower energy levels.

q: Each main shell is again divided into a number of sub-shells or ____.
e: Sub-shells (s, p, d, f) are also referred to as orbitals, representing regions of electron probability.

q: The letters used for sub-shells notations: s stands for sharp; p for ____; d for diffuse and f for fundamental.
e: The sub-shell letters originate from historical spectral line descriptions: sharp, principal, diffuse, and fundamental.

q: The maximum number of electrons in s, p, d and f sub-shells is ____, 6, 10 and 14, respectively.
e: An s sub-shell can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.

q: The shell number 1 (K shell), has only ____ sub-shell.
e: The first energy level contains only the s sub-shell.

q: The shell number 2 (L shell) has s and ____ sub-shells.
e: The second energy level introduces the p sub-shell alongside the s sub-shell.

q: The shell number 3 (M shell) has s, p and ____ sub-shells.
e: The third energy level contains s, p, and d sub-shells.

q: The shell number 4 (N shell) has s, p, d and ____ sub-shells.
e: The fourth energy level is the first to include the f sub-shell.

q: The electrons always go into the shell nearest to the nucleus which has ____ energy.
e: According to the Aufbau principle, electrons fill the lowest available energy levels first.

q: The shell which is furthest from the nucleus is called the ____ shell.
e: The outermost shell is termed the valence shell and dictates chemical reactivity.

q: The electrons in this shell are known as outer electrons or ____ electrons.
e: Valence electrons are the ones involved in forming chemical bonds.

q: These electrons are involved in ____ reactions.
e: Chemical reactions primarily involve the sharing or transfer of valence electrons.

q: The distribution of electrons in an atom of an element is called the ____ structure.
e: Electronic structure describes how electrons are arranged around the nucleus.
